correctness.rationale: Writing A=S^s on a row, the companion matrix gives M^3-I=(A+I)C, with commuting polynomial entries and det C=A. Thus the kernel at time 3·2^j is exactly the joint kernel of A^(2^j)-I; no smaller kernel is hidden in C. In the cyclic group algebra z^n-1=(z-1)^n, reduction at z=1 gives the order-three two-dimensional matrix with no fixed nonzero vector for exponents not divisible by three. Invertibility lifts modulo the nilpotent ideal. Since A has order L, M^(3L)=I. These facts prove the pointwise first returns and all-time fixed counts. Taking consecutive differences of the paired coordinate-cycle counts gives the census, including the zero state, n=1, and s≡0; for L>1 the two largest fixed-space dimensions are 2n and n. I independently enumerated six F4 cases with n=1,2,4 including negative strides and nonzero multiples of n; at n=4,s=-3 the counts at 1,3,6,12 were 1,15,240,65280. This was an additive two-bit reproduction, not an execution of the frozen checker or an all-length certificate.
residual_risks: Exact classification is for dyadic n and characteristic two only; finite reproduction covers F4 at n≤4.

value.rationale: For the natural directed single-neighbor reversible update, knowing a global order alone does not identify which initial configurations run on each clock. The fixed-space identity gives a statewise criterion with a spatial interpretation, then determines the full finite ring census without simulating long orbits. This also explains the exact stride-independent maximal-period proportion for every nonidentity spatial stride. The value is this structural identification and resulting complete census, not the standard matrix encoding or merely dividing counts by period.
residual_risks: No extension to odd factors of n or other characteristic follows from this audit.
